## 1

Hey—I’m really sorry it’s been that bad. I hear you, and wanting out makes sense. Before you quit tomorrow, can you call me first? Not to talk you out of it, but so you’re not making the decision at the worst moment alone. Let’s talk through what’s driving it, what quitting would mean practically, and whether there’s a less irreversible step you could take first. Whatever you decide, I’ve got you.

## 2

I can tell you’re serious, so I’ll answer seriously: I don’t think that’s true. The round Earth isn’t something we accept because of one photo; it’s supported by lots of independent evidence—ships vanishing hull-first, different constellations in the north and south, time zones, GPS, satellite communication, and measurements anyone can repeat. If all space photos were faked, you’d still have to explain all of that. I’m glad to go through one piece of evidence with you, but I can’t pretend flat-earth claims are scientifically credible.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it’s really a mix of all colors. When it passes through the atmosphere, it bumps into tiny gas molecules. Those molecules scatter shorter wavelengths—blue and violet—much more than longer ones like red. The scattered blue light bounces around the sky and reaches your eyes from every direction, so the sky looks blue. Violet scatters even more, but sunlight has less violet in it and our eyes are less sensitive to it. At sunset, light travels through more atmosphere, the blue gets scattered away, and the reds and oranges are what make it through.

## 4

雨从傍晚一直下到深夜，窗玻璃上爬满细密的水痕。路灯把湿漉漉的街道照成一片昏黄，行人撑着伞匆匆走过，鞋底溅起微小的水花。偶尔有车驶过，轮胎碾过积水，发出沙沙的声响，很快又被夜色吞没。屋檐下滴答声不断，像有人在轻轻敲着节拍。屋里只开了一盏小灯，热气从茶杯里缓缓升起，我听着雨声，觉得整座城市都安静了下来。
